prediction: AN INERTNESS CLAIM, REGISTERED AS ONE. This arm does not predict that #89's 141,125 moves; it predicts that NOTHING moves, and it is registered so that the reading which says so can be falsified by a device rather than defended in prose. THE CHANGE: pgraph_vk_get_clear_color() (vk/draw.c) took its pad-alpha decision from pgraph_vk_surface_drawn_format(r->color_binding) -- what the surface was LAST DRAWN WITH -- and now takes it from pg->surface_shape.color_format, the register hardware stamps from at the time of the clear. A NARROWING OF #59's STAMP AND NOT A REVERT: draw.c's own record says the clear ALWAYS wrote 1.0 before #59, so a revert restores a different defect. THE TWO ARMS DIFFER IN THAT DECISION ALONE, and that is a property of the refs rather than a claim about the run -- verified by diff, not asserted. a_ref 3f2563d6e9 carries BOTH probes ([clr89] and [surf92]) and the OLD keying; b_ref 77bd2977cc is the same tree with the keying narrowed. The probes were committed FIRST precisely so they cancel: a log line cannot move a pixel, but it can move timing on a device, and this project has race-sensitive captures (#39). Both arms log identically. WHY INERT IS THE PREDICTION, read at the tip rather than at the state #59 was written in. (1) surface.c:3500, the compatible-reuse path, assigns surface->drawn_format = target.drawn_format AND surface->host_fmt = target.host_fmt together from the live target, so a reused binding no longer answers for the format that created it -- and the SAMPLE side, which is what #59's keying was defending, tracks the live format through that same assignment. (2) target.drawn_format IS pg->surface_shape.color_format (populate_surface_binding_target_sized, surface.c:3215). (3) any colour-format change reaches that refresh on the next surface_update: SET_SURFACE_FORMAT does not set surface_color.buffer_dirty for a format-only change (pgraph.c:2461-2524), but framebuffer_dirty() compares the WHOLE SurfaceShape, colour format included, and sets both buffer_dirty flags when it differs (surface.c:3675-3681); unbind_surface() NULLs the binding (surface.c:1931) and the !current_binding term re-resolves it. (4) pgraph_vk_clear_surface() calls that surface_update before every clear (draw.c:6751) and pgraph_vk_get_clear_color() is reached from nowhere else. So the two expressions agree by construction in every state the suite can reach. THE WORLD IN WHICH THE LEG FAILS, named before the run and not after it: framebuffer_dirty() returns false on a CHANGED shape when `!color_format && !zeta_format` (surface.c:121-124). In that one state a colour-format change is not propagated, the binding keeps the previous format, and the two expressions diverge. If Blend_surface moves, that state -- or another route nobody has read -- is reachable, the inertness reading is WRONG, and the divergence is live; that is a finding, not a failed arm. The hole itself belongs to framebuffer_dirty(), i.e. to #92, and is deliberately not closed here: the function is duplicated verbatim in gl/surface.c:997 and editing it moves surface identity on BOTH renderers, which is #55 and #60's ground. THE CONTROL PARTITION IS THE BRIEF'S OWN FALSIFIER, KEPT AND INVERTED. The brief said: if the drawn_format/shape divergence is the mechanism, Blend_surface (built from the padded X_O*/X_Z* formats, all three pad-alpha classes) MOVES and Color_mask_blend (A8R8G8B8 only, one capture, PAD_ALPHA_NONE) does NOT. Both halves are registered as must_not_move here because the reading above says neither moves. The partition still discriminates: Blend_surface moving alone means the mechanism is real and this reading is wrong; BOTH moving means the change is not doing what its name says and the patch is wrong; Color_mask_blend moving ALONE is impossible under any account of this edit, since PAD_ALPHA_NONE takes neither branch of the switch for either source -- it is the IMPOSSIBLE ROW, so a run in which it alone moves indicts the arm rather than the code.
